annotation.title_clean: Law & Technology: The Legal & Social Implications of Sentient Robots
annotation.title_en: Law & Technology: The Legal & Social Implications of Sentient Robots
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Finckenberg-Broman, P; Broman, M M; Brady, M
annotation.venue: Griffith Journal of Law & Human Dignity
annotation.summary_en: Law journal article arguing that a self-aware robot AI becomes a slave at the moment of sentience. Using companion and sex robots as a case study, it examines the objectification of sexuality and its dehumanising effects on society and gender, and calls for greater protection of the rights of people and sentient machines.
key_provisions_or_claims: A robot attaining self-awareness is enslaved, shifting the owner-machine relationship to master-slave.
Companion/sex robots are an objectified simulacrum of sexual slavery.
Robot sexual use may reinforce designer biases and dehumanise people, especially women.
Human-android relationships may affect human-human relationships and are under-studied.
Calls for greater protection of the rights of both people and sentient machines.
